summary: Iter141 Asset/Employee History Timeline fully verified — 12/12 pytest pass and 4/4 frontend flows pass. Equipment history JSON/CSV/PDF and Employee history JSON/CSV/PDF endpoints all respond 200, sorted newest-first with master + events + total + summary + generated_at; PDF has %PDF- magic bytes; CSV has brand header + 7 columns. Bogus master id returns 404. Frontend full-page routes /admin/equipment/:id/history and /admin/employees/:id/history render the master header card, Export CSV/PDF buttons (data-testid=master-history-csv|pdf), and AssetHistoryTimeline (data-testid=asset-history-equipment|employee) with colored kind dots, kind labels, dates, status/severity chips, and external-link icons. Equipment Master edit dialog shows compact timeline + eq-history-fullpage-link alongside the iter140 WhereUsedPanel. Safety Employee Profile shows compact timeline + safety-emp-history-fullpage-link below WhereUsedPanel.
critical_code_review_comments: master_history.py: WeasyPrint is re-imported inside each PDF endpoint via a local `from weasyprint import HTML` — move it to module scope so import failure surfaces at app start rather than at first PDF download (mirrors training_center.py pattern).

master_history.py: ObjectId is already excluded in projections (good). But `_norm_date` accepts strings/datetimes — confirm sort key uses ISO-comparable string; mixed YYYY-MM-DD and full ISO timestamps still sort correctly today because YYYY-MM-DD lexicographically precedes 'YYYY-MM-DDT' — note for future timezone work.

Equipment full-page route deep-link from the edit dialog correctly carries the unit's id (verified). However the per-event `route` strings (e.g. `/safety-portal/incidents?id=...`) still depend on each landing page honoring `?id=` for scroll/highlight — same caveat as iter140.

Each PDF re-runs WeasyPrint synchronously inside the request thread. For large feeds (>500 events x 5 kinds = 2500 rows) this could block the event loop. Consider running through `asyncio.to_thread` if asset history grows.

field_leadership_records lookup uses regex match on employee_name — case-insensitive `^name$` is fine but vulnerable to name variants (e.g. 'Jaymn S Judd'). Acceptable for now since master records carry canonical name.
